Давно замечаю: рутинная возня с бумажками в одиночном бизнесе — отчётность, налоги, погоня за неоплаченными счетами, разговоры с HMRC — незаметно сжирает куда больше времени, чем должна бы. Поэтому я пытаюсь разобраться, что
lede.regular2: у других самозанятых — и где ИИ мог бы реально помочь, а не просто добавить ещё один дашборд, который никто не открывает.

note.body: Мне нечего вам продать. У меня есть гипотеза: в жизни каждого самозанятого в Великобритании есть хотя бы одна конкретная повторяющаяся задача, которую все ненавидят и которую никто по-нормальному не решил. Я отказываюсь написать хоть строчку продуктового кода, пока не услышу от людей, которые реально этим занимаются. Вот здесь появляетесь вы.

SurveyPage.confidentiality: Ваши ответы строго конфиденциальны. Они поступают напрямую в закрытую базу данных — никаких третьих сторон, никаких маркетинговых списков, никакой передачи. Читаю только я.

meta.title: Privacy notice — Sole Trader Discovery
meta.description: How I collect, store and use the answers you share through the discovery survey.

sections.heading: Who runs this
sections.body: This research project is operated by Dmytro Fenko (publishing as Dmitry Fenko), a UK sole trader trading as Fenko Team. I’m the data controller for everything described below. The project doesn’t meet the conditions in UK GDPR Article 37 that require a Data Protection Officer, so I haven’t appointed one — I handle every data protection matter personally. If you need to reach me about your data, write to support@fenko.dev and I’ll reply personally.

sections.heading: ICO registration
sections.body: I’m registered with the UK Information Commissioner’s Office as a data controller and pay the annual data protection fee. My ICO registration number is ZC141876. You can verify it on the public register at ico.org.uk/ESDWebPages/Search.

sections.heading: What I collect
sections.body: Only what you type into the survey: your email address, a short description of your business, how long you’ve been running it, your free-text answers to three open-ended questions, and a server-stamped timestamp recording when you ticked the consent box and which version of this notice was in force at that moment. All of it is collected directly from you when you submit the form; nothing is bought, scraped, or inferred from other sources. I don’t use analytics, cookies, fingerprinting, or session recording, and there’s no tracking script on this site. Providing this information is entirely voluntary — there’s no contract or legal obligation to participate. If you’d rather not, just don’t submit the survey.

sections.heading: Why I collect it
sections.body: To understand whether there’s a useful product to build for UK sole traders, and to contact you if I do build one. That’s the entire purpose. Your email won’t be sold, shared, or used for marketing of unrelated products.

sections.heading: Where it’s stored
sections.body: Your responses are stored in a Supabase Postgres database hosted in the EU (Frankfurt), encrypted at rest by the platform and transmitted over TLS. Supabase Inc. — the company behind the platform — is incorporated in the United States, so the transfer to them is covered by the standard contractual clauses and the UK International Data Transfer Agreement (IDTA) included in Supabase’s published Data Processing Agreement (supabase.com/legal/dpa), which provide appropriate safeguards under UK GDPR Article 46. The website is served by Vercel Inc. (US), and the serverless function that receives and validates your form submission is configured to run in Vercel’s Frankfurt region (eu-central) — so the form data is processed inside the EU before it reaches the database. Vercel publishes a Data Processing Agreement at vercel.com/legal/dpa that incorporates the standard contractual clauses and the UK IDTA as transfer mechanisms. Both Supabase’s and Vercel’s DPAs apply to this project through incorporation by reference in their standard terms — they have not been separately countersigned. If a server-side validation error occurs while you submit the form, a small fragment of your submitted answer (up to about 1,000 characters) may transiently appear in Vercel’s function logs for up to one hour before being auto-deleted; these logs are accessible only to me. Beyond the platform staff at Supabase and Vercel (who have administrative access to their infrastructure under their respective DPAs), I’m the only person who reads and analyses the data.

sections.heading: How long I keep it
sections.body: I keep your responses for as long as the project is active, plus up to 12 months after, to allow follow-up analysis and any final write-up of findings. After that, or whenever you ask, I delete your record permanently.

sections.heading: Your rights (UK GDPR)
sections.body: Under UK GDPR you have the right to: access a copy of your data; correct anything inaccurate; have your data deleted; restrict how I use it; receive your data in a portable format (e.g. a CSV); object to processing; and withdraw your consent at any time. To exercise any of these, email support@fenko.dev. I’ll respond within one month — usually much faster.

sections.heading: Lawful basis
sections.body: Consent. By ticking the box on the final step of the survey, you agree to this notice. You can withdraw consent at any time by emailing me — that triggers deletion.

sections.heading: What I don’t do
sections.body: I don’t sell data. I don’t share it with third parties beyond Supabase (the database host) and Vercel (the website host). I don’t use it to train AI models. I don’t run ads. I don’t have a marketing funnel. There’s also no automated decision-making or profiling — no algorithm makes any decision about you based on your answers.

sections.heading: Complaints
sections.body: If you think I’ve handled your data unlawfully, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the UK’s data protection regulator — the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO). You can reach them at ico.org.uk or 0303 123 1113. I’d appreciate the chance to fix things first if you email me, but you’re not obliged to.

meta.title: Cookie notice — Sole Trader Discovery
meta.description: This site uses no cookies, no tracking, and no analytics. Here’s what that means.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body: This website does not use cookies. It also does not store anything in your browser through localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, the Cache API, or any other client-side storage technology. It does not track you. It does not run analytics. It does not fingerprint your browser or device. There is no third-party script of any kind loaded on these pages.

sections.heading: What cookies are
sections.body: Cookies are small text files that a website stores in your browser to remember information about you — your preferences, session state, or behaviour across pages and visits. Many sites use them for analytics, advertising, login sessions, and A/B testing. This site does none of those things.

sections.heading: What this site actually does
sections.body: When you submit the survey, your answers are sent directly to a database (Supabase, hosted in the EU). That request does not involve cookies. Your browser does not store anything locally from this site — no entries in localStorage, no entries in sessionStorage, no IndexedDB databases, no service worker caches. There is no session token, no persistent identifier, and no tracking pixel. Under the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003 (regulation 6), consent is required for any storage of information on a user’s terminal equipment beyond what is strictly necessary for a service the user has requested — this site avoids that situation entirely by storing nothing on your device.

sections.heading: If that ever changes
sections.body: If I ever add anything that sets a cookie or loads a tracking script — for example, a login feature or basic analytics — I will update this notice first, implement a proper consent mechanism, and tell you clearly what is being used and why. Until then, this page stays exactly as it is.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.body: If you have questions about this or notice something that looks like tracking behaviour, please email support@fenko.dev.
